TR.trend: AI now takes most software rounds
TR.evidence: In January–September 2026, 77% of the 52 Italian software rounds were AI-linked, €512M or 35% of all venture capital invested. The total for the nine months was €1.465B across 210 rounds, at an average of €7M.

Exein (Rome, embedded security) reached a $1.7B valuation with a $270M Series D in Sep 2026. Domyn (Milan, formerly iGenius) is valued at about €1.7B and is financing a sovereign supercomputer mostly with debt.

TR.trend: Physical AI builds on the industrial base
TR.evidence: Generative Bionics raised a €70M seed for humanoids, Niulinx €38M for autonomous driving, Oversonic about €30M for cognitive robots. Most of them come from IIT or the two Politecnici and sell to manufacturers.

TR.trend: CDP Venture Capital is the anchor investor
TR.evidence: The state-backed fund manager is on the cap table of 20 census companies and among the leads of 14. Its €1B AI plan splits into tech transfer (€120M), start-ups (€580M) and scale-ups (€300M).
The IT4LIA AI Factory in Bologna signed a €290M system contract in Apr 2026, aimed first at start-ups and SMEs. AI4I in Turin runs an AI Foundry, and Italy is bidding for an EU AI gigafactory.

Lexroom.ai raised a €43M ($50M) Series B for legal research. Aptus.AI (banking compliance), Cato (public tenders) and Sibill (SME finance) target the same pattern: Italian-language rules and documents that general models handle poorly.

TR.trend: A broad base, a narrow funded top
TR.evidence: A national map presented in the Senate counts 14,840 AI-focused firms at end-2025. Only a few hundred have institutional venture funding, and this census profiles 74 of them.

TR.trend: Exits go to strategic buyers and to New York
TR.evidence: Qualcomm bought Arduino, TeamSystem bought Normo.ai and Stirling Square bought iConsulting. Italy's largest tech listing of the period, Bending Spoons, chose Nasdaq over Milan.
Dealroom puts the Italian tech ecosystem at about $140B in H1 2026, with venture investment up 29%, and the combined value of Italian AI companies at about $8.2B.

PO.summary: Adopted Sep 23, 2025. The first national framework in the EU alongside the AI Act. It creates a deepfake offence (one to five years), sets rules for AI at work and in healthcare, names the Bank of Italy, CONSOB and IVASS as market-surveillance authorities for finance, and delegates implementing decrees within 12 months.
Moves the high-risk obligations to Dec 2, 2027 for Annex III systems and Aug 2, 2028 for Annex I products, giving Italian vendors more time to comply.
€1B for AI within the 2024–2028 industrial plan, including a €500M AI fund that has led rounds such as Generative Bionics and Covision Media.
EuroHPC and Cineca's €290M system for Bologna, with access for start-ups, SMEs and researchers.
The EU call for up to seven AI gigafactories drew interest from 18 member states, including Italy; costs and energy supply are the open questions.

AC.facts: Genoa institute behind iCub and ergoCub; licensed its humanoid technology to Generative Bionics, which spun out with about 70 IIT engineers.
The largest academic source in the census: seven companies (Focoos AI, AIKO, Algor, Health Triage, Enerbrain, Ermes, ALBA Robot) came through the polytechnic or its incubator.
Niulinx builds on the AIDA autonomous-driving group of Prof. Sergio Savaresi; e-Novia's portfolio includes Polimi spin-offs.
Aindo, a SISSA spin-off, builds privacy-safe synthetic data for healthcare, finance and public administration.
Runs the Leonardo supercomputer and hosts the IT4LIA AI Factory, the main public compute for Italian model training.
Minerva, trained at Sapienza within the FAIR national research partnership, joins Almawave's Velvet and ASC27's Vitruvian-1 as Italian-built models.

RI.evidence: The average Italian round in Jan–Sep 2026 was about €7M. 39 of the 74 census companies are at seed and only six private ones have reached Series B or later.
Exein and Domyn hold about 54% of the disclosed capital in the census. A setback at either would change the national numbers.
CDP Venture Capital is in 20 of 74 cap tables. Private and foreign lead investors appear in fewer rounds.
Analysts question whether Italy can fund and power an AI gigafactory, given energy prices and grid capacity.
Vendors comply with both the national AI law and the EU AI Act, whose dates have moved. Implementing decrees under Law 132/2025 are still due.
At least ten Italian-founded AI companies reviewed for this census are headquartered in London, the US, Switzerland or the Netherlands, usually to raise larger rounds.
